subject: [RFC PATCH v1 0/3] iomap: convert to in-iter ->iomap_next() model

reviews.author: Fengnan
reviews.summary: Fengnan reported that enabling iomap_next mode improves performance by 1.6% when used alone, but the gain drops to around 10% after enabling simple read as well; he is still investigating issues in his current modification to support iomap_next in iomap_dio_rw
reviews.raw_body:
First, a brief update on my progress: I modified |iomap_dio_rw| so that 
the XFS direct

I/O read path can support |iomap_next| mode, and ran 4K random read 
performance tests.

Using the performance with both |iomap_next| and simple read disabled as 
the baseline,

enabling only |iomap_next| improved performance by 1.6%; enabling only 
simple read

improved performance by 7.3%; enabling both |iomap_next| and simple read

improved performance by 8.8%.

In non-|iomap_next| mode, |simple read| improves performance by about 10%.
After enabling |iomap_next|, the gain drops somewhat. The changes needed 
to make
|iomap_dio_rw| support |iomap_next| are relatively large, so there may 
be issues in my
current modification. I am still investigating why.

2026-06-29.patch_summary: This patch series converts the iomap code to use an in-iter model, where a single callback function is used for both beginning and ending I/O operations. The conversion involves merging two existing functions into one and adding a helper function to process I/O operations. An example of devirtualizing the callbacks on a hot path is also provided to avoid indirect calls through struct iomap_ops. The patch series raises questions about whether this conversion is worth it, given that indirect calls are cheap on modern hardware.
